- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then decline too sharply, missing sustained upward momentum.
- After sharp spikes in true values (e.g., 53+), model underreacts and fails to capture the full magnitude of the spike.
- Model shows weak mean reversion — fails to adjust downward when true values dip below recent highs.
- Forecasts lag behind true values by 1–3 days in the early part of the 30d window, then catch up.
- Model overcorrects after spikes, leading to premature downward revisions that don’t match true trend continuation.
- Forecasts are overly conservative in the final 10–15 days of the 30d window, underestimating late-stage price surges.
- Model exhibits “anchor bias” — anchors on recent high prices and fails to adjust for structural shifts or policy changes.
